title: Define entry contracts for third-party weight submissions to the model catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: establish a machine- and human-readable "entry contract" (manifest + tests + metadata) that third-party model weight submitters must provide to be accepted into the Redwood model catalog. Motivation: reduce runtime incompatibility incidents, make pin/release guidance deterministic, and shorten verification cycles for community-provided weights.
scope: In scope: definition of the manifest schema, mandatory and optional fields, automated ingestion checks, smoke/inference test harness, recommended soft-pin strategy and upgrade policy, and documentation for partners. Out of scope: UI catalog display changes, billing/rate-limiting policy, and full legal contract negotiation (legal will be engaged where necessary).
requirements: Provide a machine-readable manifest (YAML/JSON) with provenance: author, source URL, license, cryptographic checksum (sha256) of weights and tokenizer files.
Architecture metadata: model family, expected layer types, tokenizer name and vocabulary files, supported sequence-lengths, and checkpoint sharding layout.

Runtime compatibility tags: recommended runtime profile (e.g., 'kv-cache-friendly', 'sequence-optimized'), quantization readiness (int8/4-bit), and known incompatibilities (e.g., fused-attention-required).

Performance & footprint indicators: estimated peak VRAM for common batch/sequence configurations, typical latency/throughput numbers (measured on a specified baseline instance), and test payload used for measurements.

Validation artefacts: a minimal evaluation report (JSON) showing pass/fail on a standard smoke test (generation and embedding), sample input/output pairs, and a small regression dataset with expected outputs where applicable.
Security/legal attestations: license compatibility checkbox, export-control declaration, and optional contact for takedown/security issues.
Suggested pin policy: author-suggested soft-pin (major.minor) and a list of compatible variants; a machine-readable 'compatibility matrix' to assist auto-routing.
Upgrade/rollback notes: explicit instructions for model authors on how a runtime should fallback to older variants and the expected behavior for KV cache across versions.
Metadata for serving: recomended batching settings, cache prefixes to enable for prefix caching, and suggested kernel selection hints if available.
Testing harness: a reproducible script (or container image) that the ingestion pipeline can run to validate the model passes minimal inference checks within resource limits.
acceptance_criteria: A stable manifest JSON/YAML schema (v1) published in Confluence and a JSON Schema file committed to the repo.
Ingestion pipeline accepts a sample community submission with complete manifest and evaluation artefacts in an automated end-to-end run on CI (green pipeline).
Automated smoke tests exercise at least: tokenization roundtrip, short-sequence generation, embedding consistency, and KV-cache priming without crashing on the baseline runtime (g4dn-like profile).
Soft-pin recommendations are surfaced in the catalog entry and included in the ingestion metadata payload so routing can use them for fallback decisions.
Security/legal checklist is present and signaled to the intake flow; submissions missing required attestations are rejected with a clear error message.
Documentation and contributor-facing onboarding doc (confluence + markdown) published with migration guidance for authors of previously accepted models.
At least one partner/community test submission validated end-to-end during the rollout window (internal mirror or partner sandbox).
Metrics to track: ingestion failure rate, time-to-verify per submission, number of runtime incompatibility incidents attributed to community models.
decisions: Adopt 'soft-pin' as default: we will not force immutable pins at intake; instead we capture author-recommended pins and a compatibility matrix to allow conservative routing policies.
Manifest v1 will require cryptographic checksums and tokenizer references; non-provision of tokenizer files will fail ingestion unless the model maps to a known tokenizer in the catalog.
Baseline smoke tests will run on a single standardized infra profile to keep CI cost predictable; broader perf profiling will be optional for authors but strongly recommended.

We will surface incompatibility flags rather than block admission for non-critical metadata omissions during an initial grace period (soft enforcement), with enforcement toggles controlled by the intake policy service.
risks: Community submitters may provide incomplete or inaccurate provenance, increasing legal exposure if licenses mismatch.
Initial schema strictness may slow intake velocity and burden small community contributors—need a clear grace and remediation flow.
Relying on author-provided performance numbers risks regressions in production if tests are not reproducible; CI must enforce deterministic runs.
Complex compatibility matrices may be misinterpreted by routing; runtime team must provide clear matching semantics to avoid unintended fallbacks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): publish manifest v1 schema, implement CI smoke harness and ingestion acceptance tests; internal-only pilot with two trusted community partners.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): open intake to wider community in a sandbox environment, collect feedback, and iterate error messages and docs.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): enable soft enforcement in production with monitoring dashboards; require manifest for new catalog entries but allow remediation for existing entries.
Phase 4 (ongoing): move from soft enforcement to strict enforcement for critical fields after 90 days, based on observed ingestion metrics and partner readiness.
